# Codex fixtures

The Codex adapter's fixtures: the app-server route (`codex app-server --listen stdio://`, JSON-RPC) and the exec
fallback (`codex exec --json`), replayed by the fake CLI through the real resolver and spawn path.

**Two kinds of fixture sit side by side, both synthesized.** Some scenarios were recorded live and published in
synthesized form ("Synthesized from live recordings" below); the rest are generated from the 0.160 protocol by
`recipes/synthesize.mjs`. Every header says `"synthesized": true` with a `synthesizedFrom` note that names its source.
Every scenario has a one-command re-record recipe (below).

| What | Source |
|---|---|
| `app-server/X01b-handshake-readiness` | **Synthesized from a live recording**: codex-cli 0.160.1 (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe`), an empty temp `CODEX_HOME`, `initialize` → `initialized` → `windowsSandbox/readiness` (answered `notConfigured`). No account, no thread, no token. |
| `app-server/` X01a, X02, X03a/b, X04, X06a/b, X07, X08, X09h, X10, X12a, X17 and `exec/` E01, E02, E04 | **Synthesized from live recordings**: codex-cli 0.160.1 with a ChatGPT login on Windows (the Windows sandbox ready), each turn in a fresh `git init`-ed copy of `tests/fixtures/sandboxes/ts-small`. A pass's model is pinned to `gpt-6-luna` (the model/list default): the profile's own configured model is refused for a ChatGPT login (X09h, the one pass without a pin). |
| `app-server/` X18a, X18b | **Synthesized from live recordings**, codex-cli 0.160.1: a pass with **no** model: what the adapter sends after X09h's thread/start (`model/list{includeHidden:true}`, then turn/start with the account's default). Their replay takes X01a's list as the probe's facts (`pass.probe`). |
| read-only scenarios (X02, X09h, X12a, X17, X18a, X18b, E01) | Recorded with the read-only pass's `features.apps`, `features.plugins` and `features.hooks` = false (thread/start `config`, exec `-c`). |
| `app-server/X20-mcp-tool-approval` | **Synthesized from a live recording**: an MCP tool approval on Implement, sent as an elicitation and relayed (below). |
| `app-server/` X21, X22 | **Synthesized from live recordings**: a manual compaction (`thread/compact/start`) and an automatic one under a low limit (below). |
| `app-server/X24-compaction-steer` | **Synthesized from a live recording**: X22's automatic compaction, then the post-compaction reminder as a `turn/steer` (below). |
| `../codex-evidence/X17-catalog-refresh-two-hosts/recording.jsonl` | **Synthesized from** an earlier live X17 (before the read-only feature switches): its opened pages span two hosts, one named only in an item's results. The web-search shape tests read it; no replay does. |
| everything else under `app-server/` and `exec/` | **Synthesized** by `recipes/synthesize.mjs` |

## Synthesized from live recordings

The scenarios above that were recorded live (23 under `app-server/` and `exec/`, plus the X17 in `../codex-evidence/`)
are rewritten by `scripts/synthesize-fixtures.mjs` (its header comment has the exact rules): ids become fake `fa4e…`
ids of the same shape, times move so `recordedAt` is 2030-01-01, plan, account and rate-limit details and the
account-specific model lists are replaced, and all model text and tool output becomes fake words of the same length
(code tokens kept). The protocol, the CLI's own messages, token counts and Dim Factory's host frames stay as sent,
except values the host echoes. Each header keeps `cliVersion` (0.160.1). The same script rewrites a live recipe's
`pass.json` and notes (the thread ids a resume continues). They are listed in `FROM_LIVE`
(`tests/unit/codex/protocol/contract.test.ts`); `recipes/synthesize.mjs` does not write them.

The live originals are kept in `tests/fixtures-private/`, which is not published. `scripts/check-fixtures.mjs` and
`tests/unit/fixtures-synthesized.test.ts` fail when a published recording is not synthesized or carries account data
or live model text. Regenerate after a change to the originals or the script:

```
node scripts/synthesize-fixtures.mjs            # --only <ID>,<ID> for some, --check to compare only
DUMP_IDS=<ID>-<slug>,exec/<ID>-<slug> pnpm vitest run --project integration tests/integration/codex/adapter/expected-events.dump.test.ts
```

Locally, `DIM_FACTORY_LIVE_FIXTURES=1` runs the Codex adapter replay test on the private live recordings and their own
`expected.events.json` instead (`tests/live-fixtures.ts`).

## Protocol types

`src/core/adapters/codex/protocol/v0.160.0/` holds the output of the installed **codex-cli 0.160.1**, generated by
`scripts/gen-codex-types.mjs`. It runs only the generators, with an empty temp `CODEX_HOME`:

```
node scripts/gen-codex-types.mjs --bin "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe"
#   codex app-server generate-ts --experimental --out <tmp>/ts
#   codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental --out <tmp>/schema-experimental
#   codex app-server generate-json-schema --out <tmp>/schema-stable    (methods.json "experimental" flags only)
```

The folder has three more files besides the TypeScript: `schema/codex_app_server_protocol.schemas.json` (the
experimental bundle), `methods.json` (every method by direction, plus the watched types' fields) and `meta.json` (the
CLI version, the commands, and a content hash that a unit test checks).

**The folder name stays `v0.160.0`.** `--check` against 0.160.1 shows no difference. 0.160.1 is a patch
of the 0.160 line, and nothing in it breaks what Dim Factory relies on.

The version floor is also covered. The Desktop alpha at `~/.codex/.sandbox-bin/codex.exe` (0.147.0-alpha.6.5) has every
required method and optional capability, with no shape problem (protocol.ts `checkProtocol`).
Its schema differs only in methods and fields Dim Factory does not use, so it needs no folder of its own.

`--check` is what the weekly job runs against the latest CLI. A new folder is due only when it reports **breaking**:

- a required method is gone, or
- a watched shape broke (protocol.ts `WATCHED_SHAPES`): a property or value Dim Factory sends or reads was removed, or a
  type Dim Factory sends gained a required property.

## Layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `app-server/<ID>-<slug>/recording.jsonl` | A header, then `{t, dir, line}` frames, then the exit frame |
| `app-server/<ID>-<slug>/expected.events.json` | What Dim Factory's adapter must emit for it (below) |
| `exec/<ID>-<slug>/…` | The same for `codex exec --json` |
| `recipes/synthesize.mjs` | The generator of the synthesized fixtures and their recipes (`--check`: compare only; the unit suite runs the comparison). A live scenario is not in it: its recipe is kept by hand. |
| `recipes/<ID>-<slug>/stdin.jsonl`, `responders.json` or `responders.mjs`, `pass.json`, `record.txt` | The live re-record recipe and its command |
| `recipes/dim-factory-responder.mjs` | A `--responders` module that answers every server request exactly as the adapter does (approvals by a list of decisions, elicitations cancelled, the refused requests -32000, anything else -32601), so a recording replays whatever the live model asks for. A live recipe's `responders.mjs` is one line on top of it. |

Frames, beyond Claude's `in` / `out` / `err` / `exit`:

| Frame | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `{"dir":"eof"}` | The host closed stdin here. The replay waits for that close: exec reads its prompt to EOF, and an app-server exits once its input is gone. |
| `{"dir":"file","argvPath":"-o","content":…}` | What exec left in its `-o` file. The replay writes it where the host's argv says. |
| `{"dir":"hold"}` | The CLI was still running when the host killed it (exec has no graceful stop). The replay idles until it is killed. |

### Header

`"protocol":"jsonrpc"` (app-server) makes the fake replay by **message**, not by line:

- A recorded request takes the next client request of the same method, in any order across methods.
- A reply to a server request is matched by the server's id. Server ids are replayed as recorded, so the host must echo
  them.
- The host's own request ids are free: each recorded id maps to the one the host used, and responses carry it.
- Every match is deep-compared, with `<CWD>` and `<REDACTED>` placeholders, timestamps and nested ids masked.
- The live recordings were made before the product was renamed, so their host frames carry the former name
  (`clientInfo.name`, a refusal message that names the app). The replay masks it like an id: it binds to the name the
  host sends now, and the server's echo of the client name (`userAgent`, `originator`) is written with it
  (`RECORDED_HOST_NAMES` in `tests/fake-cli/fake-cli.mjs`). The recordings themselves keep the former name.
- A mismatch exits 99, and a host that closes stdin early exits 98.
- Any client message the recording does not have fails the replay at the exit.

`"pass"` says how Dim Factory ran the recorded process. The replay suites build `StartOptions` from it.

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `pass`, `probe` (X01b), `listModels` (X01a) or `vendorSetup` (X11b/c, with `call`, `params` and the expected `ok`) |
| `step`, `mode`, `planNative`, `prompt`, `model` | The pass; `prompt` `"<REDACTED>"` = any text (X17). `model` is the pass's own model (the ones recorded live pin `gpt-6-luna`; on exec it is the `-m` the argv carries). |
| `answers` | `[{decision, why?}]`, given to the asks in order (`why: "ask-timeout"` = the ask timer) |
| `stop` | `{after: <partial event>, reason}`: the user's Stop, once that event is seen |
| `resume` | `{sessionId, priorUsage?}`: Fix, or a resume after an ask timed out (Allow & resume); `priorUsage` is the prior pass's cumulative total |
| `allowRules`, `local`, `winSandbox`, `structured`, `route: "exec"` | As in StartOptions / the probe facts |
| `probe` | The fixture whose model/list answer is the pass's facts (`CodexFacts.accountModels`, as a probe of it leaves them): X18a/b name X01a |

### expected.events.json

As for Claude, the file mixes normalized events and the adapter signals the scenario is about, but without liveness.
Every entry is **partial**: only the fields the contract fixes.

- Events have no ask `requestId`, `expiresAt` or `detail`, and no tool `summary`.
- The comparison is `toMatchObject`: events in order against the adapter's events, signals in order against its signals
  without liveness.
- `done.usage` is this pass's delta of the cumulative totals: `input` is uncached input, and `cacheRead` and
  `reasoning` are informational.
- A recording names the sandbox `<CWD>`; the replay's own pass folder in the adapter's output reads back as
  `<CWD>` before the comparison (an agent message links files by their absolute path).

## Suites

| Suite | Covers |
|---|---|
| `tests/unit/codex/protocol/` | protocol.ts vs the schema; the generator's diff rules; every frame valid 0.160; the contract invariants and safety rules on every fixture; the failure fixtures through the classifier; the set equals the generator output |
| `tests/integration/codex/fixtures/` | every fixture replayed through the real resolver, spawn and JsonRpcPeer (strictness: wrong params 99, stray request 99, early close 98; the host's own ids); every recipe re-recorded against the fake gives its fixture back |
| `tests/integration/codex/adapter/` | the Codex adapter itself against these fixtures |
| `tests/unit/fixtures-redaction.test.ts` | every file here is redacted, every server frame is a fixed point of the Codex profile rules ("Redaction"), and no path under a temp folder is left |
| `scripts/scan-profile-leaks.mjs` (run by hand, step 4 below) | what only the recording profile names (its ids, its terms) and the machine, before a live recording is kept; its own test is `tests/unit/codex/protocol/scan-profile-leaks.test.ts` |

The weekly CI workflow (`.github/workflows/codex-weekly.yml`) needs no account and spends no token. It runs two jobs:

- **type-diff**: `gen-codex-types.mjs --check` against the latest npm CLI.
- **stdin-replay**, on Windows and Linux: every recorded host frame here is validated against the latest CLI's own
  schema (`scripts/codex-fixture-check.mjs --schema …`). Then X01b's handshake is replayed live against that CLI
  (`--live-handshake`, an empty temp `CODEX_HOME`).

Regenerate after a change to the adapter's frames (`src/core/adapters/codex/params.ts`), the refresh schema or a
scenario:

```
node tests/fixtures/codex/recipes/synthesize.mjs
```

## Re-recording live

The recorder refuses your own `~/.codex` unless told `--allow-user-codex-home`. An isolated profile is the default: `mkdir %USERPROFILE%\.codex-fixtures`, then in a terminal
`set CODEX_HOME=%USERPROFILE%\.codex-fixtures` and `codex login`. The recorder never inherits `OPENAI_*` or `CODEX_*`,
replaces the profile path with `<CODEX_HOME>` and redacts what a real profile gives away ("Redaction" below).

1. For each scenario, use a fresh `git init`-ed copy of `tests/fixtures/sandboxes/ts-small` as `<sandbox>`. Give it a
   neutral local git identity (the recorder also redacts the `user.name` it finds there). For exec, create
   `<sandbox>\.dimfactory` for the `-o` file.
2. Run the command in `recipes/<ID>-<slug>/record.txt`, filling in its placeholders, with `--out` pointing at the same
   path under `tests/fixtures-private/` (a live recording is never published). It feeds `stdin.jsonl`, which
   paces the frames with `$wait`. `$cwd` is bound to `--cwd`, and the thread and turn ids are `$capture`d from the
   answers. `responders.mjs` (or a synthesized recipe's `responders.json`) answers the server's requests,
   `--var threadId=<id>` names the thread a resume continues, and `--pass-file` writes the header's `pass`. Order: X04
   before X07, X06a before X06b, X03a before X10, E02 before E04. A resume's `pass.json` names the prior pass's last
   cumulative total as `priorUsage` (X06b also its late-allow rule).
3. Pass `--timeout 900000`: a turn takes longer than the recorder's 2-minute default.
4. Look over the recording's free text (README "Redaction") and run the review scan:
   `node scripts/scan-profile-leaks.mjs --codex-home <CODEX_HOME> --since <the recording day>`. It looks through
   `tests`, `src` and `scripts` for what only the profile names: its own ids (every id in `session_index.jsonl`, the
   `installation_id`; a v7 id from `--since` on is the recording's own), its terms and the machine (in memory, counts
   only, never `auth.json`; `--names` adds the MCP server names as whole words). It must find nothing. Then publish
   it synthesized, `node scripts/synthesize-fixtures.mjs --only <ID>`, and write its `expected.events.json` with the
   dump tool:
   `DUMP_IDS=<ID>-<slug> pnpm vitest run --project integration tests/integration/codex/adapter/expected-events.dump.test.ts`
   (exec: `exec/<ID>-<slug>`; with `DIM_FACTORY_LIVE_FIXTURES=1` the same tool writes the live copy's). A live
   recording that differs from its generated one is the point: what the adapter gets wrong is an adapter fix with a
   unit test, never an edit to the recording. Drop the scenario from `recipes/synthesize.mjs` so the generator stops
   writing it, and add it to `FROM_LIVE` in `tests/unit/codex/protocol/contract.test.ts`.
5. Run the suites.

**What the live recipes do differently from the generated ones** (each `record.txt` says so):

- **The model is pinned** (`gpt-6-luna`, the model/list default) in `thread/start` / `thread/resume` and the exec
  argv, as Dim Factory sends a picked model. The recording profile's configured model (`gpt-5.6-sol`) is refused for a
  ChatGPT login; that first X02 attempt is kept as X09h.
- **Asks need escalation.** With the Windows sandbox ready, in-sandbox commands and edits never ask. X03a/b and X06a
  ask for `npm view typescript version` (network); X04 asks for a file outside the folder; X08 starts
  `npm test -- --watch` first so the Stop lands mid-command.
- **E04's prompt is one line** (the exec prompt is one stdin line), with its finding.
- **X10 resumes X03a's thread** (the recipe's "any persisted thread with a finished turn").
- **X17's turn text is a rendered refresh prompt** (`renderRefreshPrompt` with the seed prices, the live X01a model
  list and the recording's date), now in its `stdin.jsonl`; the header's `pass.prompt` stays `"<REDACTED>"`, since the replay
  takes the prompt from `turn/start`. Its `outputSchema` is the strict form the adapter sends.

### Redaction

A recording on a signed-in profile (your own `~/.codex` only with `--allow-user-codex-home`) carries more than a temp
home does. The recorder takes it out of every line the CLI writes
(`out`, `err`, the `-o` file); the host's own frames are left as sent.

| What | Becomes | Where |
|---|---|---|
| tokens, emails, the home folder, the user name in paths, the host name, `CODEX_HOME`, the sandbox | as before (`<TOKEN>`, `user@example.invalid`, `~`, `user`, `host`, `<CODEX_HOME>`, `<CWD>`) | `src/shared/redact.ts` |
| the machine's temp folder and every path segment under it (a scratch folder names the session that made it; a sandbox path a shell cut or wrapped starts with it), any vendor | `<TMP>` | `src/shared/redact.ts` `redactTempFolder`, run by the recorder after the sandbox rule on every line the CLI writes (also in the `~` form) |
| `installationId`, account, user and ChatGPT workspace ids (any key spelling) | `<REDACTED>` (also in diagnostics, raw run logs and heal prompts) | `src/shared/redact.ts` `ACCOUNT_KEY_PATTERN` |
| the machine in `userAgent` (OS build, architecture, terminal) | `dim-factory/0.160.1 <REDACTED> (dim-factory; 0.1.0)` | `scripts/redact-codex.mjs` |
| the remote-control identity | `serverName` `host`, `environmentId` `<REDACTED>` | same |
| the plan, credits and spend | `planType` `unknown` (a valid PlanType), the amounts `<REDACTED>` | same |
| a quota window's length and reset time (`windowDurationMins`, `resetsAt`; a spend limit's `resetsAt`): the length gives the plan away, the reset dates the account's window | `0` (numbers, so the frame stays valid). Kept: each window's used percent, whether a second window exists, and the credit flags. | same |
| MCP servers: startup and elicitation names, errors and texts, tool calls (server, tool, arguments, result), a config's `mcp_servers` | `<REDACTED>` (a form schema keeps its shape) | same |
| ChatGPT apps, hooks (path, message, output), `configWarning` texts | `<REDACTED>`, `[]` or `null` (each still valid) | same |
| custom instructions (`instructions`, `developer_instructions`, `compact_prompt`, any spelling), a thread's git `originUrl` | `<REDACTED>` | same |
| what the profile's own files name: MCP server names (whole words in free text), their commands, args, URLs and env values, trusted project folders, instruction lines (`config.toml`, `AGENTS.md`, the instructions file), and the git `user.name` | `<REDACTED>` | `profileTerms` (read in memory, never written; the summary's `profile` gives counts only). A trusted folder that is `CODEX_HOME`, the home folder, the sandbox or a folder above one of them is left to the path rules (`<CODEX_HOME>`, `~`, `<CWD>`): a profile can trust its own `CODEX_HOME` (X01a, recorded before this rule, reads `"codexHome":"<REDACTED>"`). |

Every redacted frame stays valid 0.160 protocol. The rules on frames are pure and idempotent, so
`tests/unit/fixtures-redaction.test.ts` checks that each committed recording is a fixed point of them; the synthesizer
writes its server frames through them too. The profile's terms cannot be checked from the repo (they are the
recording profile's), so look over a live recording's free text before keeping it.

Known limits: PowerShell cuts and wraps a long folder in its tables (`Get-Location`, `Get-ChildItem`), so the sandbox
rule never sees it whole there. The temp-folder rule takes what starts with the temp folder (`Directory: <TMP>`,
`<TMP>` for `…\s...`); the wrapped rest of the line stays (`chpad\live\sbx\X04`; X01b's temp-folder warning reads
`<TMP>\\` the same way). A streamed delta that splits a path just after the temp folder still leaves the rest. A file
next to the sandbox whose name starts with the sandbox's (`…\X04-version.txt`) reads `<CWD>-version.txt`. X18a keeps
one such continuation (`chpad\live\sbx-X18a…`, no session id: the recorder's rules took the rest), as some Claude
recordings do; it names no one.

Some scenarios cannot be provoked on demand (X09 limits and overloads, X12c, X14), so they stay synthesized until
observed. `record.txt` says so.

**What the live recordings settled** (codex-cli 0.160.1):

- Every notification carries `emittedAtMs` (every live recording).
- `thread/started` comes after the `thread/start` response (before the `turn/start` response), and never on a resume.
  `turn/started` comes after the `turn/start` response.
- `thread/start` and `thread/resume` echo the effective sandbox (`readOnly{networkAccess:false}`,
  `workspaceWrite{writableRoots:[],networkAccess:false,…}`), the approval policy, the model and the profile's
  reasoning effort.
- `thread/resume` re-sends the restored total (`thread/tokenUsage/updated` with the prior turn's id) after its response,
  before the `turn/start` response. One total follows every model call.
- Native plan mode is accepted (no -32602 was seen, so its text is still open); the plan is a plan item.
- Codex applies **strict** structured outputs to an `outputSchema`: the non-strict refresh schema was refused with a 400
  `invalid_json_schema` ("'required' is required to include every key in properties. Missing 'aliases'") before any
  model call. The adapter now sends the strict form (`params.ts strictOutputSchema`), which the live X17
  confirmed: every optional field is answered (`aliases: []`, `deprecated: false`), and the answer parses whole.
- A web search that opens pages reports them only in the item's `results` (opaque JSON in the protocol): action
  `other`, or `findInPage` with a null `url`, never `openPage` with a url (X17). The adapter names the first page in
  the tool line ("(+N more)") and every page in a `pagesRead` meta signal, whose hosts the refresh counts as read.
  `item/started` carries no query or action yet.
- A command approval's `availableDecisions` are `accept`, an execpolicy amendment and `cancel` (no `acceptForSession`,
  no `decline`); `decline` is accepted all the same.
- Commands run through `"C:\…\powershell.exe" -Command '<script>'`; `commandActions` carry the script (exec items do
  not). File changes name absolute paths.
- An interrupted turn leaves its running command without `item/completed`.
- *(X18a/b)* turn/start's `model` overrides the model thread/start resolved, on a plain turn and in a native
  Plan (where the collaboration mode names the same model): the turn runs it, with no refusal (X09h's model is refused
  at the first model call). The only frame seen live that names the turn's model is `thread/settings/updated`, which
  comes when the collaboration mode changes (X12a, X18b) and not for a model-only override (X18a); `turn/started` and
  `thread/tokenUsage/updated` carry no model. So the adapter sends `{asked, replaced}` before the turn and the model
  used once Codex says it runs it: that settings frame naming it, or the turn's first usage total (a model call ran).
  The vendored 0.160 schema also has `model/rerouted {threadId, turnId, fromModel, toModel, reason}` (reason
  `highRiskCyberActivity`), not seen live: for this turn of a pass with no model it names the model that runs
  (`{model: toModel, rerouted: fromModel, replaced?}`) and ends the wait.
  `model/list{includeHidden:true}` lists three hidden models besides the picker's three, and no `gpt-5.6-sol`.
- A read-only pass cannot switch the user's MCP servers off without naming them (token-free live checks, not
  published): an empty `mcp_servers` table, as an argv `-c` or as thread/start `config`, merges with the
  profile's. The documented switches are per server (`mcp_servers.<id>.enabled`,
  `plugins.<plugin>.mcp_servers.<server>.enabled`) or per kind (`features.apps`, Codex's built-in apps server); that
  each works for its own kind and a wrong one fails the pass before its turn rests on probes that printed counts only
  (not recorded). The servers start with the thread, before any turn. So a read-only pass names each server the
  user's `config.toml` defines (`mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false`; mcp-isolation.ts) and its
  copy ends with `MCP_OFF_NOTE`; when that file cannot be read or followed, a name is not a safe key, or a project
  config in the pass folder defines servers (never named: Codex loads it for trusted projects only), the copy keeps
  `MCP_NOTE`. App and plugin servers are not in that file and are not switched off.
- `features.apps`, `features.plugins` and `features.hooks` exist in 0.160.1 and switch their kinds off
  (`codex features list -c features.apps=false -c features.plugins=false -c features.hooks=false`, token-free); X02
  recorded with them started one MCP server (the profile's config.toml one the recipe does not switch off) where an
  earlier X02 without them started three (with the apps and plugin servers). `multi_agent` is on by default (`codex features list`).
- *(X20)* With `tool_call_mcp_elicitation` on (0.160.1's default), an MCP tool call on a pass that may ask is approved
  through `mcpServer/elicitation/request`, not an approval method: `mode: form`, `_meta.codex_approval_kind` with the
  tool's description and `tool_params_display`, and an empty `requestedSchema`. Accepting it with `content: {}` runs
  the tool. The adapter relays exactly that shape on Implement and Fix and keeps cancelling it on read-only passes;
  any other elicitation (a form wanting input) is still cancelled.
- *(X21, X22)* Every `thread/tokenUsage/updated` carries `last` (the latest model call) and
  `modelContextWindow` (258,400 for `gpt-6-luna`). A compaction, manual or automatic, is a `contextCompaction` item
  (`{type, id}` only, no token counts); the total after it comes as a usage update whose `last` has `totalTokens` only
  (inputs 0), so the context in use reads from `last.totalTokens`, not `last.inputTokens`. The deprecated
  `thread/compacted` notification was not sent by 0.160.1 in either case. A manual compaction costs no tokens of its
  own (`total` unchanged).
- Still open: the inline vs dotted provider keys (X13); exec's exit code when killed (E06) and its stderr for an
  unknown thread (E08).

**Codex Windows sandbox procedure** (with the fixture profile):

1. X11a: readiness reports `notConfigured`, and a Review shows the downgrade. Then, still before any setup, the
   full-mode check (X11): copy `recipes/X11a-winsandbox-not-configured-review/stdin.jsonl` to a scratch file; in its
   `thread/start` line set `"sandbox":"danger-full-access"` and remove `"ephemeral":true`, and in its `turn/start` line
   ask for `Create probe.txt containing ok, then run git status.`; record it with X11a's command and `--out` pointing
   at a scratch folder (not this tree). If `probe.txt` exists in `<sandbox>` afterwards and the recording shows the
   command's output, full mode runs without the sandbox: set `FULL_WITHOUT_WIN_SANDBOX = true` and update the table
   above. Otherwise it stays unsupported.
2. X11b: `windowsSandbox/setupStart{unelevated}` passes if an edit and a command then run with no asks.
3. X11c, only if X11b fails: the user runs `codex sandbox setup --elevated --current-user` (UAC).

The procedure needs a profile whose sandbox is **not** ready. The profile the live scenarios were recorded on already
read `ready` (Codex Desktop had set it up), so X11a/b/c and the full-mode check stay synthesized, and the sandbox
chip's click path is covered by the fake (the e2e `codex-sandbox.spec.ts`, `codex-sandbox-flow.spec.ts`,
`ui-standards.spec.ts`, `ui-layout.spec.ts`). On a ready profile only the ready line can be checked ("Codex sandbox
ready", no button). The chip's live acceptance, if wanted, runs on a not-ready profile: Dim Factory launched with
`CODEX_HOME` set to the fixture profile before its X11b, or under another Windows user.

Still open, when a profile allows: the X11 procedure and its full-mode check on a not-ready profile, X13 (Ollama),
the scenarios that cannot be provoked on demand, and live recordings on macOS and Linux (the live scenarios ran on
Windows only). The replays without a probe only record the model their thread named, the `modelUsed` signal in their
`expected.events.json`.
